answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents sign ledger registrations with a cryptographic quill, staking tokens burned irrevocably if fraud is proven. Deploying identity trees via juniper hash accumulators imposes superlinear cost scaling: registering $N$ identities requires burning $O(N^2)$ stake. A sable zero-knowledge proof verifies stake depth, rendering mass identity forgery exponentially unprofitable.
